card.name: Spots where a reason clause may follow
card.fires_on: Words at the end of a clause that states a drug, condition or instruction, where a 'because' explanation could come next. Seen after drug names, 'present', 'is', or a comma.

modes.label: After drug interaction clause
modes.description: Ends a clause naming a drug or herb in a caution or contraindication, where a reason may follow.
modes.example: Co-administration is contraindicated with St. John's w<<ort>>.

modes.label: Comma before a reason
modes.description: A comma after a noun in a precaution, directly before 'because'.
modes.example: Potassium supplements should be used cautiously in patients who are using salt substitutes<<,>> because most of the latter contain substantial amounts

modes.label: Condition-present clause end
modes.description: Verb or word ending a conditional clause like 'is present'.
modes.example: Activated charcoal should be avoided if an ileus<< is>> present; the conventional dose is 1

card.writes: It makes the word 'because' (and Chinese equivalents) more likely to come next.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence has just stated a caution or fact and a 'because' explaining why could follow.
